cancer_indication: Breast cancers harboring oncogenic NTRK1/2/3 gene fusions (rare; enriched in secretory breast carcinoma).
moa: Entrectinib is an ATP-competitive inhibitor of TRKA/TRKB/TRKC (NTRK1/2/3) as well as ROS1 and ALK. In NTRK fusion–positive breast cancers, it inhibits the constitutively active TRK fusion kinase, shutting down downstream pro-growth signaling (including RAS–MAPK and PI3K–AKT–mTOR) and promoting cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Entrectinib has central nervous system penetrance, supporting activity in brain metastases when present.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_NTRKS.description: Neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase signaling mediated by TRKA/TRKB/TRKC, which can activate downstream cascades that promote proliferation and survival.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_NTRKS.interpretation:
In breast cancer cases with NTRK fusions, TRK signaling functions as a dominant oncogenic driver and defines a biomarker-selected, targetable dependency.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In NTRK-fusion–positive breast cancers (most commonly secretory carcinoma with ETV6–NTRK3, but also rare non-secretory cases), the TRK pathway is constitutively activated and functions as the dominant oncogenic driver. Entrectinib potently inhibits TRKA/B/C and leads to high, durable response rates in NTRK-fusion solid tumors, including breast, when TRK signaling is active and untreated.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In breast cancers with oncogenic NTRK1/2/3 fusions (e.g., secretory carcinoma with ETV6–NTRK3), high TRK-pathway output reflects oncogene addiction, so TRK blockade is highly effective.
NCT02568267 (STARTRK-2); DrugBank:DB11986; ChEMBL:CHEMBL1983268; PMC TNBC NTRK platforms: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8418219/
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with an NTRK fusion signature, co-dominant parallel drivers (e.g., strong HER2/ER signaling) or marked intratumor heterogeneity can dilute TRK dependence and reduce benefit from TRK inhibition alone.
NCT02568267; FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf; DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Apparent “low” bulk TRK signaling can still be compatible with response if the fusion is present but expressed in a subclone that drives progression (e.g., metastatic focus) and is pharmacologically suppressible.
NCT02568267; NCCN patient guidance (metastatic breast; NTRK fusion → larotrectinib/entrectinib) https://www.mbcalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/stage_iv_breast-patient.pdf
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In typical breast cancers without an NTRK fusion driver, TRK signaling is not the tumor’s dependency, so entrectinib has little tumor-intrinsic target to exploit.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf; DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Entrectinib directly inhibits TRKA/B/C kinase activity, functionally downregulating TRK fusion signaling and collapsing downstream proliferative/survival pathways, enabling tumor regression in NTRK-fusion breast cancer.
NCT02568267; DrugBank:DB11986; FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even when TRK is inhibited, tumors can persist via off-target bypass (e.g., MET amplification) or strong downstream reactivation (MAPK/PI3K), yielding resistance despite TRK-pathway suppression.
Ann Oncol (MET bypass) cited in report; NCT02568267; Drug resistance review links in report (e.g., https://pathsocjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/path.6341)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: A TRK inhibitor cannot increase functional TRK signaling; any “up” is a measurement artifact or reflects more TRK+ tumor cells remaining rather than drug-induced activation.
DrugBank:DB11986; FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (on-target failure): Apparent TRK signaling persistence after dosing is consistent with NTRK kinase-domain mutations or target escape that prevents adequate inhibition, maintaining the driver pathway.
Resistance mechanisms review links in report; next-gen TRK inhibitor context noted in report; DrugBank:DB11986

HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.description: A gene-expression program reflecting increased RAS pathway output, commonly converging on MAPK/ERK-driven proliferation and survival.
HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation:
RAS/MAPK output is a key growth axis downstream of TRK and can also represent a compensatory proliferative route in TRK-driven tumors.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- If an NTRK-fusion breast tumor also harbors activating RAS/MAPK lesions (e.g., KRAS/NRAS/BRAF mutations, MEK1 alterations) or a high KRAS/MAPK signature, the tumor can maintain ERK signaling independent of TRK, blunting the effect of entrectinib. Convergent MAPK activation is a well-described resistance mechanism to TRK inhibition in multi-tumor series and in entrectinib-treated models; the same biology would predict primary/early resistance if present at baseline in breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In NTRK-fusion breast cancers, TRK fusions can strongly activate RAS–MAPK output; high KRAS/MAPK signature can therefore mark TRK-driven oncogene addiction and predict sensitivity if it is TRK-dependent.
NCT02568267; DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If KRAS/MAPK output is driven by an alternate lesion (e.g., KRAS/NRAS/BRAF activation) rather than TRK, MAPK can bypass TRK inhibition and confer resistance (cross-cancer resistance paradigm, applicable to breast).
Cell Rep (TRK+MEK strategy / MAPK resistance): PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low baseline MAPK output (no MAPK-driver co-alteration) can increase single-driver reliance on TRK fusions, improving depth/durability of response when TRK is inhibited.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low KRAS/MAPK signature together with absent TRK dependence (no NTRK fusion) implies neither TRK nor MAPK is the actionable dependency → entrectinib is unlikely to work.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf; DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective TRK inhibition should downregulate downstream RAS–MAPK signaling, preventing proliferation and supporting response in TRK-addicted breast tumors.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Bulk MAPK signatures can fall after treatment because of tumor shrinkage, yet resistant subclones may survive via PI3K/MET/ERBB bypass not captured as MAPK-high at the transcript level.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; NCT02568267

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Transient MAPK induction can reflect stress/inflammation early on, but durable sensitivity generally requires MAPK suppression; sustained “up” is not a typical sensitive state.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK reactivation (KRAS/BRAF/MEK pathway re-engagement) is a major acquired resistance route that restores proliferation despite TRK blockade (cross-cancer; relevant to breast if it occurs).
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: A survival and growth signaling program driven by PI3K activation, AKT signaling, and mTOR pathway output.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation:
PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling is a major downstream survival pathway engaged by TRK fusions and can support continued tumor viability when activated by additional lesions.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- When the PI3K–AKT–mTOR axis is not already activated by independent genomic events, the tumor is more reliant on NTRK → PI3K/AKT signaling. Entrectinib then effectively shuts down both MAPK and PI3K branches, favoring apoptosis. Preclinical TRK-driven models show strong pro-apoptotic effects when PI3K/mTOR is not independently activated, and dual TRK + PI3K/mTOR blockade further deepens responses.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In TRK-driven breast tumors, PI3K–AKT–mTOR activity can be high as a downstream arm of the TRK fusion, so tumors may still be sensitive if this PI3K output is TRK-dependent and collapses with TRK inhibition.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If PI3K is independently activated (e.g., PIK3CA mutation/PTEN loss), it provides a TRK-independent survival route and can blunt apoptosis, reducing entrectinib efficacy in breast cancer.
Report pathway table (PI3K bypass) plus DrugBank MoA: DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low baseline PI3K backup (intact PTEN; no PIK3CA activation) increases reliance on TRK fusion signaling, making TRK blockade more lethal.
NCT02568267; DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If PI3K is low because the tumor is not TRK-addicted (and instead relies on other programs), entrectinib remains ineffective without an NTRK fusion driver.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf; DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: TRK inhibition should attenuate PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling when PI3K activity is downstream of TRK fusions, promoting cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in responsive breast tumors.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even if bulk PI3K signatures drop, resistance can persist via MAPK reactivation, MET bypass, or apoptotic blockade, yielding non-response despite partial PI3K suppression.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; Ann Oncol MET bypass cited in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Short-lived compensatory PI3K feedback can occur after RTK inhibition, but durable sensitivity typically requires net pathway suppression; sustained PI3K “up” is usually unfavorable.
DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent/induced PI3K–AKT–mTOR activity (PIK3CA/PTEN/IGF axis) maintains survival despite TRK blockade and is a canonical bypass resistance mechanism applicable to NTRK-fusion breast cancer.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_MET.description: HGF/MET receptor signaling that activates downstream proliferative and survival pathways, including MAPK and PI3K signaling modules.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_MET.interpretation:
MET signaling represents a clinically relevant alternative RTK axis that can sustain growth in TRK-driven contexts when activated as a bypass route.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- MET amplification or overexpression reactivates RAS–MAPK and PI3K–AKT independent of TRK. MET amplification has been directly documented as a mechanism of acquired resistance to entrectinib in ROS1+ NSCLC, and TRK-i reviews highlight MET as a recurrent bypass node. If such MET activation exists at baseline in an NTRK-fusion breast tumor, entrectinib monotherapy is unlikely to produce deep or durable responses.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Baseline MET pathway expression can be high without being functional driver; if MET is not activated (no amplification/HGF-driven signaling), tumors may still respond if TRK is the true dependency.
Ann Oncol MET bypass cited in report; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MET activation/amplification provides a strong bypass to restore MAPK/PI3K signaling independent of TRK, predicting resistance to TRK inhibition in a breast tumor under selective pressure.
Amatu et al., Ann Oncol (MET amplification resistance) cited in report; resistance review link: https://pathsocjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/path.6341

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low MET signaling at baseline reduces availability of a major bypass track, increasing the likelihood that TRK-fusion tumors remain dependent on TRK and respond.
Amatu et al., Ann Oncol cited in report; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If the tumor lacks an NTRK fusion driver, low MET does not create sensitivity—entrectinib still has no relevant target dependency in most breast cancers.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Entrectinib does not directly inhibit MET, but effective tumor regression and reduced microenvironmental HGF/MET signaling can coincide with response as bypass pressure is minimized.
Amatu et al., Ann Oncol cited in report; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MET can appear “down” in bulk while resistance is mediated by another bypass (e.g., ERBB/PI3K/MAPK) or on-target NTRK mutation, producing failure despite low MET output.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; resistance review link in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (as drug-effect): Entrectinib is not a MET agonist; MET upregulation is not a direct therapeutic mechanism for sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired MET amplification/HGF-driven activation is a documented off-target resistance route that restores downstream survival signaling despite TRK inhibition (cross-cancer; relevant to breast).
Amatu et al., Ann Oncol cited in report; resistance review link: https://pathsocjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/path.6341

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: A gene-expression program encompassing intrinsic and extrinsic apoptotic machinery and execution pathways.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation:
Apoptotic competence influences whether tumor cells undergo effective cell death when oncogenic survival signaling is inhibited.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Tumors with intact apoptotic machinery can rapidly execute apoptosis once TRK signaling is shut off. In TRK-inhibitor models, responders show strong induction of cleaved caspases and apoptosis gene signatures after treatment; the clinical pattern of deep, rapid regressions in many NTRK-fusion tumors is consistent with this “primed” state. Baseline apoptotic competence is therefore a positive modifier of entrectinib sensitivity.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: A “primed” apoptotic state (intact TP53/pro-apoptotic readiness) makes TRK-addicted breast tumors more likely to execute rapid cell death once TRK survival signaling is removed.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even if some apoptosis genes are high, dominant anti-apoptotic buffering (e.g., MCL1/BCL2 dependence) or strong bypass signaling can prevent effective execution after TRK blockade.
Report apoptosis resistance concept; DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low baseline apoptosis signatures in a TRK-addicted tumor can still convert to apoptosis after potent TRK suppression if downstream survival signals collapse sufficiently.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong anti-apoptotic programming (apoptosis execution suppressed) is a generic resistance state that can allow persistence even when upstream oncogenic signaling is inhibited.
Report pathway table (apoptosis down → resistance); DrugBank:DB11986

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Successful TRK inhibition reduces MAPK/PI3K survival signals and shifts cells toward apoptosis (caspase activation), correlating with response in TRK-fusion tumors.
DrugBank:DB11986; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some resistant tumors show partial cell death while surviving subclones expand via bypass pathways; bulk “apoptosis up” can coexist with net clinical resistance due to clonal selection.
NCT02568267; resistance review link in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In deep responders with rapid tumor clearance, late sampling can show fewer dying tumor cells (apoptosis signature lower) despite sensitivity (timing artifact).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce apoptosis after TRK blockade (e.g., persistent anti-apoptotic signaling, TP53 loss context) produces drug tolerance/persistence and clinical resistance.
DrugBank:DB11986; report apoptosis resistance concept

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: A transcriptional program associated with loss of epithelial features and acquisition of mesenchymal traits, including increased motility and cellular plasticity.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation:
EMT-like states in breast cancer can be linked to broader drug tolerance and signaling rewiring, potentially altering dependence on the original oncogenic driver.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- EMT-high states generally correlate with reduced dependence on a single RTK, lower proliferation, increased drug-tolerant persisters, and activation of alternative RTKs (AXL, FGFR, MET). TRK-resistance reviews list EMT and lineage plasticity as non-genetic resistance mechanisms; although most data are from other tumor types, an EMT-high signature in NTRK-fusion breast cancer would plausibly predict shallower or shorter responses to entrectinib.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some NTRK-fusion tumors may express EMT programs yet remain TRK-addicted; if TRK is still the dominant driver, they can respond despite partial mesenchymal traits.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: EMT-high states are associated with drug tolerance and alternative RTK usage (e.g., AXL/FGFR/MET), which can reduce dependence on TRK and predispose to resistance (cross-cancer; plausible in breast).
Lin et al., Nature (EMT/TKI tolerance; HNSCC context) cited in report; resistance discussion in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: An epithelial, less-plastic baseline can indicate a more dependency-driven state (TRK-addicted) and reduced availability of phenotypic escape routes, supporting sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: EMT-low does not create sensitivity without the target dependency; non–NTRK-fusion breast tumors remain resistant to entrectinib regardless of EMT status.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A transient stress-response EMT-like transcriptional shift can occur during tumor remodeling, but durable sensitivity generally requires continued suppression of oncogenic signaling and cell kill.
Resistance discussion in report; NCT02568267
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Under drug pressure, selection for EMT/mesenchymal persister cells can enable survival via alternate pathways and decreased proliferative dependence, producing acquired resistance (cross-cancer; relevant to breast if observed).
Lin et al., Nature cited in report; resistance discussion in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Responding tumors can show reduced EMT signatures as the malignant compartment shrinks and epithelial differentiation re-emerges, accompanying sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: EMT can appear low in bulk while resistance is mediated by on-target NTRK mutations or ERBB/MET/PI3K bypass, yielding progression without an EMT-high phenotype.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; resistance review link in report

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Signaling through ERBB family receptors (including HER2/ERBB2 and EGFR) that activates proliferative and survival pathways such as MAPK and PI3K.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation:
ERBB pathway activity is a major breast cancer growth axis and can co-exist with, or dominate over, other drivers in rare dual-driver settings.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In a HER2-positive breast cancer that also carries an NTRK fusion, HER2 amplification often remains the dominant driver of PI3K/MAPK signaling. In such a setting, TRK inhibition alone may not fully suppress downstream growth pathways; clinically, HER2-addicted tumors generally require HER2-directed therapy. Thus, baseline high HER2 activity is expected to blunt the benefit of entrectinib monotherapy, unless HER2 is co-inhibited. Evidence is extrapolated from multi-driver RTK settings and tumor-agnostic TRK-i series rather than from large NTRK+ HER2+ BC cohorts.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Mild ERBB signaling can coexist with TRK addiction; sensitivity can persist if ERBB is not the dominant driver and TRK fusion remains the main dependency.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: HER2/EGFR pathway upregulation (e.g., HER2 amplification or strong ERBB output) can dominate growth and sustain PI3K/MAPK despite TRK inhibition, implying need for co-targeting in breast cancer.
Report HER2/ERBB resistance concept; FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low ERBB signaling reduces a key parallel RTK escape route, increasing the chance that TRK-fusion tumors are single-driver dependent and responsive.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In the absence of an NTRK fusion, low ERBB does not create a TRK dependency; entrectinib remains ineffective in most breast cancers.
FDA label (212725) https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/212725s011lbl.pdf

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Entrectinib does not directly inhibit ERBB receptors, but ERBB pathway output can decline indirectly if the tumor mass and autocrine growth-factor signaling decrease during response.
NCT02568267; DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ERBB signaling can be low while resistance is driven by MET/MAPK/PI3K bypass or on-target TRK mutations, leading to progression without ERBB activation.
PMID:32755586 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32755586/; resistance review link in report

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (as therapeutic effect): Entrectinib is not expected to increase ERBB signaling as a mechanism of tumor kill; ERBB upregulation is not a sensitivity mechanism for TRK inhibitors.
DrugBank:DB11986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive ERBB activation (HER2/EGFR upregulation) can provide a compensatory RTK signal that restores PI3K/MAPK and drives resistance unless ERBB is co-inhibited (breast-relevant in HER2+ contexts).
Report HER2/ERBB resistance concept; NCCN patient guidance link in report: https://www.mbcalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/stage_iv_breast-patient.pdf

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal) Subtype: NTRK fusions are extremely rare in luminal breast cancers, but they have been identified. Some ER+ breast cancers acquired NTRK fusions after progressing on hormonal therapy, suggesting a subclone with an NTRK fusion may emerge and drive the tumor. If an ER+ cancer is driven by an NTRK fusion, it will respond to entrectinib, but optimal care might require combined endocrine therapy to suppress any residual ER-driven component.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive Subtype: NTRK fusions are similarly uncommon for HER2-positive disease. A reported case described a HER2-enriched breast adenocarcinoma with an ERBB2–NTRK3 fusion and HER2 amplification, implying two drivers. There is no published report of treating such a case with entrectinib; the discussion extrapolates that dual targeting would likely be needed, as entrectinib alone could be insufficient if HER2 signaling remains unchecked.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): TNBC is the subtype where NTRK fusions, while still rare, are slightly more encountered aside from secretory carcinoma. True NTRK fusions were described as exceedingly rare in non-secretory TNBC; one TNBC cohort case was reclassified as secretory carcinoma with an NTRK3–ETV6 fusion. Secretory breast carcinoma (often ER/PR/HER2-negative) is defined by ETV6–NTRK3 and has shown very high response rates to TRK inhibitors; scattered non-secretory TNBC case reports with NTRK fusions also support responsiveness. TNBC may have higher likelihood of MET amplification as a resistance mechanism, so vigilance for MET is noted.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA-mutated / HRD+ Subgroup: No known correlation between BRCA1/2 mutations and NTRK fusions is described; they appear independent. If both were present, the text discusses potential dual susceptibilities (PARP inhibitors for BRCA and TRK inhibitor for the fusion), but no reported case is described.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like vs. Other Intrinsic Subtypes: The text notes secretory carcinoma does not fit neatly into typical intrinsic subtypes and that there is not enough data to say intrinsic subtype affects response; the determinant is presence of the targetable NTRK abnormality.
